title: An angel restores the authority to baptize
setting: Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery were translating the Book of Mormon at Harmony, Pennsylvania. Joseph’s later history says the text raised a question about baptism for the remission of sins. On 15 May 1829 the two men went into the woods near the Susquehanna River to pray about it. They reported that an angel who called himself John, the Baptist of the New Testament, ordained them. This section is the ordination wording as recorded in Joseph’s history, written years later.
summary: These are the words of an ordination, not a full revelation. The speaker calls Joseph and Oliver his “fellow servants.” He confers the Priesthood of Aaron in the name of Messiah. He says this priesthood holds the keys of the ministering of angels. It also holds the keys of the gospel of repentance and of baptism by immersion for remission of sins. He says it will not be taken from the earth until the sons of Levi again offer an offering in righteousness.

contextNote.title: Authority tied to a specific task
contextNote.text: Joseph and Oliver had read about baptism for the remission of sins and wanted to know more. Verse 1 answers with authority rather than with instructions. It names three things this priesthood holds keys to: angels’ ministering, the gospel of repentance, and baptism by immersion. The last of these matches their question about baptism for remission of sins. The verse also looks forward, saying the authority will remain until the sons of Levi offer again. That phrase echoes Malachi 3:3, which Moroni had also quoted. Here “keys” means the right to perform and direct these specific acts.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 12–17 and Joseph Smith—History 1:66–75 presents this ordination as the restoration of the Aaronic Priesthood. Verse 1 lists three keys; how does each one connect to what Joseph and Oliver were seeking that day?
reviewNote: Read the single verse. Official heading gives near Harmony, 15 May 1829, Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery, and the angel’s statement that he acted under Peter, James, and John. JSP Study Companion lists the source as an excerpt from JS History, 1838–1856, vol. A-1. The page for page 17 (May 1829) loaded, but the fetch tool did not show the transcription. Woods, Susquehanna River, and the baptism question are from Joseph Smith—History 1:68–72. The Malachi echo is an editorial cross-reference, not from the heading. Fact-check 2026-10-12: contextNote claimed they “had no one to baptize them” and that all three keys matched their question; neither is in the heading or history. Reworded to the documented question about baptism for remission of sins.
